title: I am the one who saw the army coming.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ as a clear warner
then: Ibn Kathir cites the two Sahihs: the Prophet ﷺ compared himself to {idea}a man who saw an army with his own eyes and ran to his people saying escape, escape{/idea}. Some left by night and were saved; {trap}others stayed until morning and were overtaken{/trap}.
now: Your friend texts you: the road is flooded, take the other way. Your mother says: that man is bad news. {idea}A warning is someone who saw what you cannot, and cared enough to run and tell you.{/idea}
old: People who warn me are just being negative.
new: A clear warner is someone who saw the danger and loved me enough to say it.
try: Thank one person who warned you about something, even if you did not listen at the time.

title: They swore oaths together to oppose the truth.
subtitle: The Muqtasimin, the ones who made a pact
then: Ibn Kathir says the Muqtasimin {trap}made a pact to oppose, deny, and insult the Prophets{/trap}. He compares it to Salih's people, who swore to one another to attack him by night, citing 27:49. It is as if they took an oath for everything they denied.
now: The group chat agrees, before the meeting, to shut down the new idea no matter what. The family agrees to freeze someone out. {trap}Deciding together to reject something before hearing it{/trap} is an old pattern. {idea}You can refuse to join it.{/idea}
old: If the group agrees, I should go along.
new: A group pact to reject the truth is still a rejection, and I do not have to sign it.
try: Next time a group decides against someone before hearing them, ask to hear them out first.

title: They cut the Quran into pieces to reject it.
subtitle: Sorcerer, poet, madman: labels instead of listening

key.label: Two ways to break it up

then: Ibn Abbas said this meant {trap}believing in some of the Book and rejecting some{/trap}. Another report says it was Quraysh before Hajj season: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah rejected every label, admitted the words were sweet, then {trap}they agreed to call him a sorcerer{/trap}.
now: Someone says something true that stings. Instead of thinking about it, you reach for a label: they are just jealous, just emotional, just old-fashioned. {trap}A label lets you skip the message.{/trap} {idea}Listen first.{/idea}
old: Once I have put a label on something, I know what it is.
new: Labels are often a way to avoid hearing a truth; the Quran asks to be heard whole.
try: When you catch yourself labeling someone to dismiss them today, listen to them for one more minute.

title: By your Lord, every one of them will be asked.
subtitle: An oath that all will be questioned
then: Allah swears by Himself that all of them will be questioned. Ibn Kathir reports Abu Al-Aliyah: {idea}all people will be asked about two things: what they used to worship, and what their response was to the Messengers{/idea}.
now: Your boss asks for a quick update and your heart races. Imagine the two questions that really matter. {idea}What did you give your heart to? How did you respond when the message reached you?{/idea} You can prepare those answers today.
old: Nobody is really going to ask me about my life.
new: Everyone will be asked what they worshipped and how they answered the messengers, including me.
try: Write down your honest answer to both questions, and keep it somewhere private.

title: Not did you do it, but why did you.
subtitle: The question about everything they used to do
then: Ibn Abbas linked this to 55:39, where no one is asked about their sin. He explained: {idea}they will not be asked, did you do such and such, because Allah knows better. He will say, why did you do it?{/idea}
now: You snapped at your child, skipped the prayer, sent the harsh email. You already know you did it. {idea}The question waiting is why.{/idea} Ask yourself now, while you can still change the answer.
old: As long as no one finds out what I did, I am fine.
new: Allah already knows what I did; what I will be asked is why.
try: Tonight, pick one thing you did today and ask yourself honestly why you did it.

title: Say it openly now, and do not be pulled aside.
subtitle: The end of secret preaching
then: Ibn Masud said {idea}the Prophet ﷺ was practicing and preaching secretly until this verse was revealed; then he and his Companions came out into the open{/idea}. Ibn Kathir cites 68:9: {trap}they wished that you would compromise{/trap}.
now: At work you skip your prayer or hide it in a storeroom so nobody asks. With friends you water down what you believe so it does not get awkward. {idea}You can be calm and still be open about who you are.{/idea}
old: Keeping my faith quiet keeps everyone comfortable.
new: There comes a point to stop hiding what I stand for and live it openly, with calm.
try: Do one small act of faith openly today that you would usually hide.

title: Allah will handle the mockers for you.
subtitle: Sufficiency against those who ridicule
then: Ibn Ishaq names five leading men of Quraysh whose mockery went to extremes. Ibn Kathir says the verse means {idea}do not fear them, because Allah will suffice you against them and protect you{/idea}, citing 5:67. {trap}Each of those five mockers came to his end soon after.{/trap}
now: Someone at work mocks your fasting, your hijab, your beard, your halal lunch. You lie awake writing comebacks. {idea}You do not have to win every exchange.{/idea} {reward}Allah is enough for you.{/reward}
old: If I do not answer every insult, I lose.
new: Allah is enough against the mockers; my job is to keep going, not to win every argument.
try: Let one mocking comment pass today without a reply, and say hasbiyallah instead.

title: Putting another god beside Allah, they will come to know.
subtitle: A warning that ends in knowing
then: The mockers are described: {trap}those who make another god along with Allah{/trap}. Ibn Kathir calls the ending, they will come to know, {trap}a strong warning and grave threat{/trap} to those who set up other deities.
now: Not idols on a shelf. Your career, your image, your phone, a person you cannot say no to, the thing you check first in the morning and last at night. {idea}Ask what sits beside Allah in your heart.{/idea}
old: Shirk is something only idol-worshippers do.
new: Anything I give the place that belongs to Allah can become a god beside Him.
try: Notice the first thing you reach for when you wake tomorrow, and put remembrance of Allah before it.

title: We know your chest feels tight from what they say.
subtitle: Allah sees the Prophet's distress

row.title: seen and known
sub: even the Prophet ﷺ felt it

then: The surah introduction says the Prophet ﷺ had grown {trap}a little tired{/trap} after years of rejection. Here Allah says {idea}We know your breast becomes tight because of what they say{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says: do not let that weaken your resolve; trust Him.
now: You read the comments under your post. You overhear what your in-laws said. Your chest tightens and stays tight all evening. {idea}Allah knows that exact feeling.{/idea} {reward}He said so to His most beloved.{/reward}
old: If words hurt me this much, my faith must be weak.
new: Allah sees the tightness words cause; feeling it is human, and He meets it with care.
try: When hurtful words weigh on you today, tell Allah exactly how it feels.

title: The cure for a tight chest is praise and prostration.
subtitle: What to do with the pain
then: Right after naming the pain, Allah gives the remedy. Ibn Kathir says: {idea}keep yourself busy with remembering Allah, praising Him, glorifying Him and worshipping Him{/idea}. He cites a hadith: {reward}four rakat at the start of the day, and I will take care of you until its end{/reward}.
now: After the hurtful call, you scroll for an hour to numb it. It does not help. {idea}Try the prescription instead: stand up, wash, pray two rakat, stay in sujud a little longer.{/idea}
old: When I am hurt, I need distraction.
new: When my chest is tight, praise and prostration are where Allah tells me to go.
try: The next time you feel hurt today, pray two rakat and make your sujud long.

title: Worship your Lord until the certainty comes.
subtitle: The last verse: worship has no finish line before death
then: Salim bin Abdullah said {idea}the certainty means death{/idea}. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ telling Umm Al-Ala about Uthman bin Mazun: {reward}the certainty has come to him, and I hope good for him{/reward}. Worship continues as long as the mind is sound, in whatever way a person is able.
now: You had a strong Ramadan and coasted after. You did Hajj and felt finished. Or you are sick and think worship is not for you anymore. {idea}It keeps going, in whatever form you can manage{/idea}, until the last day.
old: There is a point where I have done enough worship.
new: Worship is a lifelong companion, in whatever shape I can manage, until death comes.
try: Choose one small act of worship you can keep doing daily for the rest of your life, and start today.
